subject: Opsly POC — capacity, latency tradeoffs & GPU selection
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@opsly.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Opsly POC — capacity, latency tradeoffs & GPU selection

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clear traffic profile and the two target SLAs (p95 < 120ms for inline suggestions, batch reranks allowed up to 500ms). Per our discussion I captured the initial sizing hypotheses and a short list of follow-ups so we can finalize a Dedicated capacity recommendation for the POC.

Quick summary of what I heard:
- Peak TPS: ~220 TPS for short-turn interactive endpoints (avg prompt ~80 tokens, response ~40 tokens)
- Batch rerank job: 18 TPS equivalent (5–7s jobs) running in off-peak windows
- Token mix: ~60% short prompts (<200 tokens), 40% long-form (500–2000 tokens) for occasional summarization
- Primary concern: keep p95 for interactive under 120ms while minimizing committed spend

Open items for us:
1) Confirm whether Opsly expects steady-state 220 TPS sustained vs burstable over 10–15 minute windows.
2) Clarify whether the long-form summarization can be routed to a cheaper model variant (quantized) or must be the same model as inline suggestions.
3) Confirm acceptable GPU preference (A100 family vs H100) — Opsly mentioned existing infra familiarity with A100.

Next steps I propose:
- We will run a quick throughput model matrix (attached) with two hardware profiles (A100-40GB and H100-80GB) and three concurrency plans (low/medium/high) to show p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
- Set a short technical call tomorrow to review the matrix and pick a target for the POC commit.

I've attached a blank TPS/token matrix for you to confirm sample distributions; I populated it with the numbers you gave on the call.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
[Attachment: opsly_poc_tps_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)]

From: Samir Khan <samir@opsly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@opsly.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Opsly POC — capacity, latency tradeoffs & GPU selection

Thanks Ben — this is great context. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 220 TPS is bursty: we expect spikes up to ~220 for 5–10 minute windows but sustained target is ~120 TPS.
- Long-form summarization can be run on a cheaper quantized variant — prefer not to impact inline model if we can route.
- We are currently standardized on A100s for our infra team, but happy to evaluate H100 if cost delta is reasonable.

Procurement side: I copied our procurement contact (procure@opsly.com). We will need an outline of the committed capacity, expected monthly spend, and whether Redwood supports mid-term SKU swaps (e.g., start with A100 and move to H100 if latency/cost tradeoffs are better).

We can take the matrix offline — I'm good for a quick 30m sync Tuesday 10am PT.

Samir
Head of Platform, Opsly

Ben — forwarding a short note from infra about concurrency knobs to include in the matrix. Vivek suggests we add a third column showing estimated KV cache hit rate impact for short prompts (that will materially reduce tokens and effective TPS). Also recommends highlighting recovery behavior if a GPU flavor is unavailable (auto-fallback to smaller batch sizes + model variant).

Key technical bullets to add to the doc:
- Continuous batching impact on p95 for short prompts (include modeled p95 delta at 0%, 25%, 50% prefix caching)
- Token budget effect: estimate tokens/sec per GPU at different quantization profiles (8-bit vs 4-bit)
- Failover plan: policy to route to hosted API for burst > sustained capacity or emergency failover

I'll add a page to the attached PDF with the infra notes.

Laura
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samir / procurement team — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming the bursty profile.

Recap and agreed next steps:
- We will present two committed capacity proposals tuned for your burst profile: (A) A100-focused baseline that optimizes cost with moderate concurrency and (B) H100-focused baseline that prioritizes p95 with higher single-GPU throughput.
- Matrix deliverables (attached): estimated p95 by endpoint, cost per 1k tokens, expected token/sec per GPU, and failover policies. Laura included infra notes on caching and quantization effects.
- Logistics: 30m sync Tuesday 10am PT to walk the matrix and pick a POC commit. After you pick a path, Redwood will produce a short draft MSA addendum for the reserved pool and a one-page ops runbook for the POC.

Action items for Opsly:
- Confirm if procurement needs vendor info or an initial SOW before the sync.
- Confirm whether Opsly legal wants any specific data residency language for the POC.

If you want, I can also include a third hybrid proposal that starts on A100 and includes a committed option to migrate to H100 mid-term (we support controlled SKU swaps with 30d notice).

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Ben
